sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: The effect of drowsiness on wudu and prayer
sources.supports: Drowsiness while retaining awareness does not invalidate wudu; includes Hanafi, Maliki, Shafii and Hanbali quotations, with a Maliki heavy/light distinction. This is not a complete four-school posture comparison.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham: Does light sleeping break the wudhu?
sources.supports: Cited Hanafi account distinguishes firmly seated buttocks from reclining or dependence on support such that removing it would cause a fall.

sources.title: Sunan Abi Dawud 200: Wudu from sleeping
sources.supports: Anas reports the Companions dozing while waiting for Isha, then praying without renewing ablution. The page gives an al-Albani grading of sahih.

review.notes: Read the captured Arabic Dar al-Ifta answer, the Hanafi institutional answer and Abi Dawud 200. The Maliki contrast and Ibn Qudamah uncertainty statement are explicitly attributed. No diagnosis, invented scholar review, app CTA or duplicate how-to-wudu intent. Three main headings, practical examples and existing generated purity hero follow the user’s simplification request.
